main.title: Crackdown
main.subtitle: A city to grow into
main.summary: Crackdown is Realtime Worlds' 2007 open-world action game for Xbox 360. An enhanced Agency operative takes on the gangs controlling Pacific City. Gunfights, driving and rooftop exploration develop alongside the agent's growing abilities, gradually changing which parts of the city can be reached and how its opposition can be handled.

cards.heading: A city to grow into
cards.text: Crackdown is Realtime Worlds' 2007 open-world action game for Xbox 360. An enhanced Agency operative takes on the gangs controlling Pacific City. Gunfights, driving and rooftop exploration develop alongside the agent's growing abilities, gradually changing which parts of the city can be reached and how its opposition can be handled.

cards.heading: The next roof
cards.text: Agility Orbs draw attention upwards. A glow on a roof suggests a sequence of ledges, signs and nearby buildings that might lead to it. Improving agility makes longer jumps possible, turning a route that once seemed out of reach into another opportunity. The city changes through the character's abilities: the buildings remain where they were, but travelling between them becomes a different experience.

cards.heading: Learning through action
cards.text: Strength, firearms, explosives and driving improve through use. A player who spends time fighting at close quarters develops a different immediate advantage from one practising with weapons or vehicles. Those abilities give ordinary objects another role in a confrontation. A car can be transport, cover or something a sufficiently strong agent can turn against an enemy.

cards.heading: Another agent in the city
cards.text: Gang leaders give the open city targets to pursue, while rooftop races and scattered discoveries compete for attention between confrontations. A second agent can join the campaign cooperatively. The pair has room to explore and approach an objective from different positions, bringing the pleasure of an unlikely jump or an improvised attack into a shared journey through the city.

main.title: Crash of the Titans
main.subtitle: A defeated enemy becomes the next set of moves
main.summary: Crash of the Titans is Radical Entertainment's 2007 action platformer for PlayStation 2, Wii and Xbox 360, with a PSP conversion by SuperVillain Studios. Neo and Nina Cortex are turning the islands' creatures into powerful mutants. Crash and Aku Aku fight back by taking control of these enemies and using their abilities against the next obstacle.

cards.heading: Crash borrows a bigger body
cards.text: Crash of the Titans is Radical Entertainment's 2007 action platformer for PlayStation 2, Wii and Xbox 360, with a PSP conversion by SuperVillain Studios. Neo and Nina Cortex are turning the islands' creatures into powerful mutants. Crash and Aku Aku fight back by taking control of these enemies and using their abilities against the next obstacle.

cards.heading: Taking over the encounter
cards.text: Crash first weakens a mutant with punches, kicks and combinations. Once it is stunned, he can climb aboard and direct its movements. The creature supplies a different reach, attack pattern or special power, changing how the surrounding fight works. Smaller opponents become easier to manage from a stronger body, while another large enemy can provide the next opportunity to switch. Choosing the moment to take control gives a battle its shape.

cards.heading: A path between fights
cards.text: The routes also call for jumping, rope swinging and stretches of movement between combat areas. Aku Aku can serve as a board for sliding along parts of the course. These sections change the pace before another encounter fills the path with enemies. Mojo collected along the way improves Crash's fighting abilities, so progress comes through both learning a creature's moves and expanding the attacks available when Crash is on his own.

cards.heading: Sharing the journey
cards.text: A second player can enter as Carbon Crash, sharing the route and helping with the same groups of enemies. The two characters can combine their actions, including one riding the other, so cooperation becomes part of the physical comedy. The console game places its emphasis on extended encounters and changing bodies.

main.title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Justice for All
main.subtitle: The Lie Leaves the Courtroom
main.summary: Phoenix Wright investigates four new cases, with Psyche-Locks bringing the search for contradictions into conversations outside court.

cards.heading: Phoenix returns to court
cards.text: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Justice for All reached Nintendo DS in North America on January 16, 2007, following the Japanese Game Boy Advance original. Phoenix returns to investigate four cases and defend his clients in court. The new Magatama reveals Psyche-Locks around secrets, giving evidence a role in questioning people before a trial begins.

cards.heading: Investigation supplies the evidence
cards.text: Each case moves between investigation and trial. Phoenix visits locations, questions witnesses and gathers evidence in the Court Record. In court, the player compares testimony with those discoveries, looking for a contradiction that can be proved. An object collected earlier may become decisive only after a witness makes a particular claim.

cards.heading: Breaking the Psyche-Locks
cards.text: Psyche-Locks appear when a character conceals a subject. Presenting the right evidence breaks the locks and opens further conversation. Incorrect answers reduce a life bar, so questioning people during an investigation carries a risk similar to presenting evidence in court. The Magatama makes hidden information visible while leaving the player to work out how to uncover it.

cards.heading: Franziska and the pressure of a trial
cards.text: Prosecutor Franziska von Karma brings an aggressive new presence to the courtroom, alongside returning characters including Maya and Edgeworth. Witnesses turn questioning into theatrical confrontations. The life bar gives different mistakes different penalties, while some cases place Phoenix in uncomfortable moral situations: finding a contradiction also means deciding when and against whom to use it.

main.title: Etrian Odyssey
main.subtitle: A guild at the forest entrance
main.summary: Etrian Odyssey is Atlus and Lancarse's Nintendo DS dungeon role-playing game about a player-created guild exploring the Yggdrasil Labyrinth. A first-person view shows the route ahead while the touchscreen holds a map that the player must draw and annotate. The party advances in measured steps, returning to town to rest, prepare and develop its members. The approach gives exploration a patient, practical character. Progress means understanding a place well enough to record it, then judging whether the party can safely push beyond the point already reached.

cards.text: Etrian Odyssey is Atlus and Lancarse's Nintendo DS dungeon role-playing game about a player-created guild exploring the Yggdrasil Labyrinth. A first-person view shows the route ahead while the touchscreen holds a map that the player must draw and annotate. The party advances in measured steps, returning to town to rest, prepare and develop its members. The approach gives exploration a patient, practical character. Progress means understanding a place well enough to record it, then judging whether the party can safely push beyond the point already reached.

cards.heading: The map is part of the equipment
cards.text: The stylus marks paths and places symbols on a grid as the party discovers the labyrinth. A useful note can identify a door, a resource or a route that will matter when supplies are lower. The map is therefore something the player makes alongside the characters' improvement. An inaccurate drawing can complicate the return journey, while a careful one supports the next expedition. Etrian Odyssey uses the DS's second screen to restore a personal record of discovery, putting the familiar role-playing map back into the explorer's hands.

cards.heading: Some enemies are better avoided
cards.text: Powerful wandering FOEs occupy the labyrinth alongside ordinary encounters. Their movements advance with the party's actions, making a corridor's layout important before combat begins. Several can converge if the party remains in a dangerous position. Building a five-person team from different classes gives the player choices in preparation, but those choices do not make every visible threat a sensible target. The party's abilities and the map work together: understanding where an enemy can move may preserve the expedition more effectively than winning another difficult fight.

main.title: Hotel Dusk: Room 215
main.subtitle: A Mystery Held Like a Book
main.summary: Cing asks players to hold Nintendo DS like a book as Kyle Hyde investigates the guests and secrets of a small hotel.

cards.heading: Kyle Hyde checks in
cards.text: Cing's Hotel Dusk: Room 215 reached Nintendo DS in North America on January 22, 2007. Kyle Hyde enters a hotel while searching for a missing person and gradually uncovers connections between its guests. The console is held vertically like a book, with conversations and investigation spread across its two screens. Drawn, rotoscoped characters give the mystery the appearance of a moving noir sketchbook.

cards.heading: An adventure held like a book
cards.text: One screen can show Kyle's conversation partner while the other presents text, the room or an object being examined. The stylus and other DS features also help solve tactile puzzles. After Another Code, Cing continued looking for ways to connect adventure games with the handheld's hardware; holding Hotel Dusk like a book made its long conversations part of that design.

cards.heading: Characters drawn from filmed performances
cards.text: Cing filmed actors and used rotoscoping to turn their gestures into drawn animation. Dark outlines and light fills keep expressions readable during conversations. The slight movement of each sketch gives Kyle's exchanges a distinctive rhythm, with the faces taking up one side of the open console.

cards.heading: Following the guests' secrets
cards.text: Kyle searches rooms for objects and clues, but much of the investigation takes place in conversation. He must connect incomplete accounts and decide when to press a guest further. Asking a question too early can harm the exchange. Returning to a room after learning a secret changes the meaning of the people and objects already encountered there.

main.title: Picross DS
main.subtitle: A picture hidden inside a grid
main.summary: Picross DS is Jupiter's Nintendo DS collection of nonogram puzzles, where numbered clues describe the filled squares needed to reveal a picture. The player works between rows and columns, marking cells as occupied or empty until the image becomes clear. The stylus gives this quiet process a direct surface, while progressively larger puzzles demand more careful comparison. Each completed grid offers two kinds of satisfaction at once: the logic has been resolved and the apparently abstract marks have turned into something that can finally be recognised as a small image.

cards.heading: A picture hidden inside a grid
cards.text: Picross DS is Jupiter's Nintendo DS collection of nonogram puzzles, where numbered clues describe the filled squares needed to reveal a picture. The player works between rows and columns, marking cells as occupied or empty until the image becomes clear. The stylus gives this quiet process a direct surface, while progressively larger puzzles demand more careful comparison. Each completed grid offers two kinds of satisfaction at once: the logic has been resolved and the apparently abstract marks have turned into something that can finally be recognised as a small image.

cards.heading: A clue describes a run of squares
cards.text: Numbers alongside a row or column describe groups of consecutive filled cells, with spaces separating one group from the next. Comparing the available length with those groups reveals where a square must belong or remain empty. A deduction in one direction can then resolve an uncertainty in the other. Normal mode identifies mistakes and adds time penalties, encouraging a careful reading before committing to a cell. The most useful action may be marking an empty square, because removing a possibility can provide the information needed to complete the next line.

cards.heading: The collection can include a personal puzzle
cards.text: Puzzle creation allows players to design their own pictures, while the original online features provided ways to share them, download classic grids and compete over solving speed. Daily challenges offer another short routine alongside the main collection. Difficulty grows through larger arrangements and more demanding relationships between clues, giving the same basic rule a substantial range. Picross DS makes the handheld useful as a small puzzle book, with the additional pleasure that an image devised by a player can become a problem for somebody else to solve.

main.title: Professor Layton and the Curious Village
main.subtitle: An inheritance hidden in riddles
main.summary: Professor Layton and the Curious Village is Level-5's Nintendo DS puzzle adventure introducing Professor Hershel Layton and his young assistant Luke. They visit St. Mystere to investigate the Golden Apple, an heirloom connected to the late baron's fortune. The village's residents share a remarkable fondness for puzzles, making a conversation as likely to produce a brainteaser as a clue. Animated sequences and an illustrated setting connect these individual challenges into a mystery. Solving one question becomes a way of earning another piece of the village's attention.

cards.text: Professor Layton and the Curious Village is Level-5's Nintendo DS puzzle adventure introducing Professor Hershel Layton and his young assistant Luke. They visit St. Mystere to investigate the Golden Apple, an heirloom connected to the late baron's fortune. The village's residents share a remarkable fondness for puzzles, making a conversation as likely to produce a brainteaser as a clue. Animated sequences and an illustrated setting connect these individual challenges into a mystery. Solving one question becomes a way of earning another piece of the village's attention.

cards.heading: The answer is under the stylus
cards.text: The player taps people and objects to investigate the village. A puzzle may call for a number, a marked area, a sequence of movements or another form of touchscreen response. Its value is measured in picarats, while hint coins can purchase progressively more helpful clues. Time is available for thought; committing to an incorrect answer can reduce the reward. The different inputs let a collection of traditional brainteasers feel comfortable on the DS, with the stylus serving as both an investigating finger and a pencil.

cards.heading: A village worth examining twice
cards.text: Hidden puzzles and hint coins reward attention to the illustrations, giving an apparently decorative corner a possible use. Unsolved puzzles that become inaccessible can reappear at Granny Riddleton's shack, keeping the larger collection approachable as the story advances. Rewards also supply pieces for small activities in Layton's trunk, including a robotic dog and arrangements for the visitors' rooms. These details make the village feel hospitable to curiosity. The central mystery provides direction, but the small pleasure of noticing something gives the player a reason to linger.

main.title: Monster Hunter Freedom 2
main.subtitle: Prepare for the creature before entering its territory
main.summary: Monster Hunter Freedom 2 is Capcom's PSP action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 22 February 2007. It builds a new handheld campaign around material from Monster Hunter 2, adding content and giving players another cycle of preparation, hunting and equipment-making. Large creatures provide the central encounters, each demanding observation of movement and habits rather than a simple exchange of damage. The hunter returns with materials that can improve the next expedition. A familiar monster therefore remains useful beyond its first defeat, becoming part of the work needed to confront something more dangerous.

cards.heading: Prepare for the creature before entering its territory
cards.text: Monster Hunter Freedom 2 is Capcom's PSP action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 22 February 2007. It builds a new handheld campaign around material from Monster Hunter 2, adding content and giving players another cycle of preparation, hunting and equipment-making. Large creatures provide the central encounters, each demanding observation of movement and habits rather than a simple exchange of damage. The hunter returns with materials that can improve the next expedition. A familiar monster therefore remains useful beyond its first defeat, becoming part of the work needed to confront something more dangerous.

cards.heading: The next weapon begins with the previous hunt
cards.text: Quests range from early gathering tasks to fights against one or more large monsters. Preparation matters because the equipment carried into the field determines how the hunter can respond once the target is found. Repeated encounters reveal the moments when it is safe to approach and those when distance is more valuable than another attack. Materials and rewards connect those lessons to better tools. The player grows through both kinds of progress: the character acquires equipment, while the person holding the PSP becomes more capable of reading the creature in front of them.

cards.heading: A foundation for the handheld phenomenon
cards.text: Yasunori Ichinose directed the project and Ryozo Tsujimoto produced, with music by Masato Kohda, Akihiko Narita and Yuko Komiyama. Western editions followed in August and September 2007. Local cooperative hunts made the portable format especially important, allowing a group to prepare and confront the same creature together. The expanded Monster Hunter Freedom Unite later built on this foundation. Freedom 2 remains a distinct step in that development, turning the second console game's material into a campaign whose repeated hunts and shared play fit naturally into the habits formed around the PSP.

main.title: Peggle
main.summary: Peggle is a casual puzzle video game developed by PopCap Games.

cards.text: Peggle is a casual puzzle video game developed by PopCap Games. Initially released for Microsoft Windows and Mac OS X systems in 2007, it has since had versions released for Xbox Live Arcade, PlayStation Network, the Nintendo DS (with the help of Q Entertainment), Windows Mobile, iOS, Zeebo, and Android; the game has also been ported as a Java application, and an extended minigame incorporated into the massively multiplayer online game World of Warcraft. A sequel was released in September 2008, titled Peggle Nights. PopCap, a subsidiary of Electronic Arts, announced Peggle 2 at E3 2013.

Inspired by pachinko and bagatelle, each level of Peggle challenges the player to shoot a limited supply of balls at a field of colored pegs to clear out specifically marked pegs while attempting to achieve a high score through skilled shot planning. Special powers associated with a diverse cast of cartoon "Peggle Masters" can be activated to aid the player in this task. Peggle initially sold slowly but was boosted by the inclusion of a specially designed demonstration in Valve's The Orange Box, and has since been downloaded over 50 million times.

main.title: God of War II
main.summary: God of War II is a 2007 action-adventure game developed by Santa Monica Studio and published by Sony Computer Entertainment (SCE).

cards.heading: Kratos challenges Zeus
cards.text: Santa Monica Studio released God of War II for PlayStation 2 on March 13, 2007. After defeating Ares and becoming the God of War, Kratos is betrayed and killed by Zeus. The Titan Gaia saves him from the Underworld and sends him to the Sisters of Fate, whose power offers a way to reverse the betrayal. Greek mythology provides the setting for his revenge.

cards.heading: Blades, magic and puzzles
cards.text: The gameplay is similar to the previous installment. It focuses on combo-based combat which is achieved through the player's main weapon—the Blades of Athena—and secondary weapons acquired throughout the game. It features quick time events (QTEs) that require players to quickly complete various game controller actions to defeat stronger enemies and bosses. The player can use up to four magical attacks and a power-enhancing ability as alternative combat options. The game also features puzzles and platforming elements. Compared to its predecessor, God of War II features improved puzzles and four times as many bosses.

cards.heading: Reception and the continuing trilogy
cards.text: God of War II received critical acclaim and won PlayStation Game of the Year at the 2007 Golden Joystick Awards. It sold 4.24 million copies by June 2012. The first two games returned together in the remastered God of War Collection, initially released for PlayStation 3 in 2009. God of War III continued the story in 2010.
